To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transformation of Schistoma mansoni cercarie to schistosmula is associated with the synthesis of proteins of Mr 60 000 and 58 000.

(i) a protein of Mr 60 kD and a protein of Mr approximately 58 kD are synthesized in Schistosoma mansonii cercariae in response to a temperature increase from 23 to 37 or 42 degrees Celsius, (ii) the synthesis of these proteins is confined to the initial period of transformation from cercariae to the schistosomal stage, (iii) the Mr 60 kDa protein is not synthesized in the schistosomal or egg stages

the temperature-induced proteins in S. mansoni schistosomules, schistosomule larvae that have been transformed from the cercarial stage by temperature increase, are not homologous to those found in other stages of this parasite.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis for the transformation of cercariae to the schistosome stage.
the response of S.mansoni cercariae and other stages of the parasite to temperature change.
the identification and characterization of proteins that may be involved in the transformation of S. mansooni cercariae to the mammalian stage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mr 60-58,000 proteins are unique to cercariae and are induced by temperature increase.
S. mansoni is a heat-shock protein-deficient organism and that the Mr 60 and 58, 000 proteins are unique to this stage.
the Mr 60 and 58 kDa proteins are induced in response to temperature change and that these two proteins are unique to the cercarial stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mr 70 kDa heat shock protein is not expressed by cercariae but is expressed by other stages of the parasite.
the transformation of cercariae to the schistosome stage in S. mansoni is a unique event in the parasite's life cycle and is associated with the synthesis of two heat-induced proteins.
the temperature-induced changes in gene expression during cercarial transformation are unique to this stage of the parasite and do not involve a heat shock response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Mr 70kDa protein is not induced in cercariae in response to temperature increase, and this is the first time this has been shown for a parasite.
S. mansoni, like other metazoans, has a heat shock response.

the Mr 60K and 58K proteins are induced in cercariae by the temperature shift from 23 degrees to 37 degrees C, but not by a shift to 42 degrees C, which is the normal body temperature for the mammalian host.
